new_statements.rule_in_words: For the Manus group of Admiralty languages (Smythe's Group 3, which includes Yiru = Nali as language 3A4c), the main position of word accent is the final syllable, with 'mixed' (neither clearly stress- nor syllable-timed) rhythm. This is a group-level generalization across some two dozen Manus languages, not a Nali-specific description.
new_statements.exceptions: None for accent in Table 1 (other rows carry per-language exceptions such as 'except in Ponam', 'except in Sisi', showing the table is meant to hold group-wide unless flagged). The paper's only language-specific stress note (n.13, p.1232) concerns Gele' (Kele): phonemic stress tending to long vowels, penult of reduplications, and otherwise final syllables. Blust's 1975 Nali field transcriptions (RB2-011 pp.20-33, held by the project) show final stress ticks on most numerals but initial/penultimate ticks on several disyllabic nouns, so the Nali facts may be less uniform than 'final'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level 'main position of accent' in a typological feature table compiled by a fieldworker who collected wordlists for all Admiralty languages (1940s-50s); no definition of domain, no examples for Nali. The Nali-specific SIL Organised Phonology Data (2 pp., archive 42320, 2011) would supersede this but could not be downloaded.
new_statements.identity_note: Smythe 1970 refers to Nali as 'Yiru' (language 3A4c; villages Rossun, Lauis, Yiru, Kapor, Sirra, Sonilu, Bulihan, Katin, Bua, Malei = the Nali area of SE Manus, glottocode nali1245), but his accent statement is made for his whole Group 3 (all Manus and adjacent-island languages), not for Yiru individually. Blust's 1975 notebook data are from Lahan village (speaker Pokanas Popat), also Nali proper. The unfetched SIL OPD is catalogued under Nali [nss].

Also re-read the existing-statement source: and the text layer (l.265 'main position [of accent]: penultimate | initial | final') confirm the group-level 'final' for Group 3; and RB2-011 p.20 confirms the notebook's stress ticks (numerals 2-10 and 100 ticked before the last syllable; 'songuy pe? si? 11, 'susu?, 'pwese?, 'poyo?, 'Kamew with earlier stress), primary data with no prose rule, as the reader said.
